question: What is the lubricating fluid found between the two bones at a movable joint called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Synovial fluid**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Synovial fluid is the lubricating fluid found between the two bones at a movable joint.
 
• It reduces friction between the articular cartilage of synovial joints during movement.
 
• This fluid is essential for the proper functioning of joints and helps in smooth and painless movements.
 
• Synovial fluid also supplies nutrients and removes metabolic wastes from the cartilage cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options provided are not correct for this question:
 
• **Interstitial fluid:** This is the fluid that surrounds the cells in tissues.
 
• **Cerebrospinal fluid:** This fluid surrounds the brain and spinal cord.
 
• **Amniotic fluid:** This is the fluid that surrounds a fetus within the amniotic sac.
 
• Synovial fluid is specifically found in joint cavities and is crucial for joint health.
